clue.text: Chased snipers having blown hole in the wall

indicators.note: something blown is wrecked or exploded, so the letters of the first two words are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Gunmen pursued until their hiding place is blown apart by explosives in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Hole in the wall is British slang for a street cash machine set into a building's exterior.

clue.text: Reliable policeman prospered keeping clear of drink

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the teetotal letters sit within the word for prospered

parts.note: to boom is to thrive, prosper
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A dependable officer who did well while staying off the booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper-bottomed means thoroughly sound and trustworthy, from ships sheathed in copper.

clue.text: Vice of heartless Lothario

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the letters are drawn from inside the next two words

explanation.surface: A sin typical of a callous womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth, laziness, is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Award for end-of-year speech

parts.note: Dec is December, the year's final month
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A prize given for a New Year's Eve address.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration is a medal or honour conferred on someone.

clue.text: Some fishing equipment catching trout finally, a hard problem

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, as a net holds a fish

parts.note: a sinker is a weight on a fishing line

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Angling gear landing a trout, yet still a tough challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is informal for something very difficult, such as a tough exam question.

clue.text: Like some verse, say, Alice gets excited about

indicators.note: excited about means stirred around, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Alice gets worked up over a particular kind of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes mournful verse, as in an elegy or lament.

clue.text: Special forces — hard band

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, a British special forces regiment
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Elite troops forming a tough unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: Police barrier catches a bold criminal in possession of precious stone

indicators.note: the stone holds the other pieces inside it, as one possesses something

parts.note: rock is slang for a diamond or gem

indicators.note: criminal suggests wrongly arranged, so the word bold is scrambled

explanation.surface: A police checkpoint catches a daring crook carrying a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadblock is a barricade set up by police to stop traffic.

clue.text: Aliens enter telling me to get knotted

indicators.note: knotted means tangled, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Visitors from space arrive and rudely tell someone to get lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Little green men is the jokey stock phrase for extraterrestrials.

clue.text: Ban expert writer

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A call to bar a skilled author from publishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe something is to forbid it officially, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Indian mystic travelled through water to reach island

parts.note: to travel through water is to swim; past tense swam
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A holy man swims out to an island, like a pilgrim's tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, an ascetic holy man.

clue.text: It can put out article about Queen? On the contrary

indicators.note: about means surrounding, one piece placed around the other
on the contrary reverses the stated roles: the Queen goes around the article, not the article around the Queen

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a word framing royalty, then a reversal of who wraps whom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' tells the solver to swap the roles 'about' states, so the royal abbreviation is the outer piece. 'It can put out' means knock out, as an anaesthetic does.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic: it can knock a patient out, i.e. put them out.

clue.text: Fool told to join up

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word for fool is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a nit (nitwit) is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot being instructed to enlist in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to unite or join together, as broken bones knit.

clue.text: Report on one late old item

parts.note: a bit is a small item or piece

explanation.surface: A newsroom note about someone who was tardy, flagged as an old story.
explanation.definitionFit: An obit (obituary) is a newspaper report on someone recently deceased.

clue.text: I put on a show with one Italian character entertaining president

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding a guest inside

parts.note: Mario is an Italian name, as in the video-game plumber

explanation.surface: A stage claim: I staged a show with an Italian hosting the president.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and finances theatrical productions, so would say these words.

clue.text: Support son beset by one running out of control

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the son's letter sits inside the runaway

parts.note: a bolter is a horse that runs off uncontrollably
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son swamped by a runaway who needs help.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or reinforce, like a long pillow.

clue.text: Failing to start sleeping, being clumsy

indicators.note: failing to start means losing the opening letter

parts.note: slumbering means sleeping

explanation.surface: A dozing person failing to get going, moving awkwardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbering means moving heavily and awkwardly, an adjective of clumsiness.

clue.text: Old rogue on TV's energy to write

parts.note: Compo was the scruffy old rascal in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine; with the possessive S
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A television scoundrel's vigour put into authorship.
explanation.walkthrough: Compo is the scruffy old rascal in Last of the Summer Wine, a long-running BBC comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose is to write music or verse, a plain synonym.

clue.text: High-spirited girl almost reaching US city means to gamble

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tomboy is a boisterous girl
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A lively girl heading off to Las Vegas or similar to bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle drum, a lottery device, so a way of gambling.

clue.text: Road material, a tar spread round both ends of path

indicators.note: spread round means wrapped around another piece

parts.note: a salt and a tar are both old words for a sailor

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Surfacing a footpath by spreading tar along it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' looks like part of the material; here it is a sailor, SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the bitumen mix used to surface roads.

clue.text: Match perhaps for attacking footballer

definitions.meaning: a match is one example of something struck to make fire
a forward whose job is to score goals

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a football game suits a centre forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A striker is both a thing that strikes, like a match, and a goal-scoring forward in football.

clue.text: Short article shows team meeting lawyers

parts.note: a side is a sports team
the bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: A brief news item on a football club meeting its legal advisers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidebar is a short piece printed alongside a main news story.

clue.text: Ordinary writer, quite accessible

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary (as in O level)
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An everyday author who is very approachable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open is fully available, with nothing barring access.

clue.text: Murphy gets Northern Irish party's backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the party's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A man called Murphy wins support from a Belfast political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is not a person: it is slang for a potato, a nod to Irish surnames.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy and spud are both informal words for a potato.

clue.text: Plant from south facing border

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
an edge is a border or rim

explanation.surface: A gardener's flower bed on the southern side of a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant of marshy ground.

clue.text: Went out with American lawyer then Irish priest

parts.note: DA is a district attorney in the US
Father Ted is the Irish priest of the TV sitcom

explanation.surface: A romance with a US attorney followed by one with a clergyman from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is a British sitcom about priests on an Irish island.
explanation.definitionFit: To date someone is to go out with them romantically.

clue.text: A female Wimbledon champion once

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: Apparently a woman who once won at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A female' seems to describe the champion, but Arthur Ashe, who won in 1975, was a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe won the men's singles title at Wimbledon in 1975.

clue.text: Grand works using Oriental images

parts.note: E stands for east, hence oriental
pics is short for pictures, images

explanation.surface: Large-scale artworks drawing on Eastern imagery.
explanation.definitionFit: Epics are long, grand-scale works, such as heroic poems or sweeping films.

clue.text: Rare ombu tree initially cultivated here?

definitions.text: Rare ombu tree initially cultivated here?

indicators.note: cultivated suggests ground worked over, so the letters are dug up and replanted in a new order
initially means only the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Is this where an unusual South American ombu tree is grown?
explanation.walkthrough: The ombu is a South American tree; the whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical garden devoted to growing trees, so rare species are cultivated there.

clue.text: Trade no longer carried out in conurbation

indicators.note: carried out read as taken out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Business no longer conducted in a sprawling city.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater London is the large metropolitan area of the UK capital, a vast built-up region.
